Architecture flowchart TD subgraph Submission & Control Client["Web API / CLI / Batch Submitter"] -->|SubmitAsync| Backend["IAgentRunBackend (SqliteAgentRunBackend)"] Backend -->|Transactional Write| Table[("SQLite WAL Store")] end subgraph Worker Pool WorkerService["AgentRunWorkerService"] -->|ClaimAsync| Table Table -->|AgentRunLease + FencingToken| WorkerService WorkerService -->|RenewLeaseAsync Heartbeat| Table WorkerService -->|ExecuteAsync| Handler["IAgentRunHandler"] Handler -->|Completed / WaitingForInput| Result["AgentRunHandlerResult"] Result -->|CompleteAsync / WaitForInputAsync / RetryAsync| Table end 1. Configuring the Durable Worker Host Register the SQLite backend, your IAgentRunHandler implementations, and the Generic Host worker service: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting; using MyAgents.Core.Execution; using MyAgents.Runtime.Workers; using MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite; var builder = Host.CreateApplicationBuilder(); // 1. Register SQLite persistence backend with optional scope throttling builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAgentRunBackend>(_ => new SqliteAgentRunBackend( databasePath: "agent-runs.db", options: new AgentRunBackendOptions { MaxLeasedRunsPerScope = 4, MaxOutstandingRunsPerScope = 100 })); // 2. Register your run handler(s) builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAgentRunHandler, DataProcessingAgentHandler>(); // 3. Register the hosted worker service builder.Services.AddMyAgentsRunWorker(options => { options.WorkerId = Environment.MachineName; options.MaxConcurrentRuns = 4; options.IdlePollInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(250); options.LeaseDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30); options.LeaseRenewalInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10); options.BaseRetryDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2); options.MaximumRetryDelay = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5); }); using var host = builder.Build(); await host.RunAsync(); 2. Implementing IAgentRunHandler Each IAgentRunHandler declares a stable HandlerId and implements ExecuteAsync(AgentRunContext, CancellationToken): using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Execution; public sealed class DataProcessingAgentHandler : IAgentRunHandler { public const string StableHandlerId = "data-processing"; private readonly IAgentSessionFactory _sessionFactory; private readonly AgentDefinition _definition; public DataProcessingAgentHandler( IAgentSessionFactory sessionFactory, AgentDefinition definition) { _sessionFactory = sessionFactory; _definition = definition; } public string HandlerId => StableHandlerId; public async ValueTask<AgentRunHandlerResult> ExecuteAsync( AgentRunContext context, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { // Optionally inspect or save intermediate checkpoints during multi-step work if (context.CheckpointJson is null) { await context.SaveCheckpointAsync("""{"stage":"started"}""", cancellationToken); } await using var session = _sessionFactory.CreateSession(context.RunId, _definition); var turn = await session.InvokeAsync( [AgentMessage.FromText("user", context.InputJson)], cancellationToken); var output = turn.Output.LastOrDefault()?.Content ?? string.Empty; return AgentRunHandlerResult.Completed(output); } } Pausing a Run for External Input (WaitingForInput) A handler can pause a durable run and release its worker slot while waiting for a human or webhook signal: // Inside ExecuteAsync: if (context.ResumeInputJson is null) { return AgentRunHandlerResult.WaitingForInput( checkpointJson: """{"step":"awaiting-manager-signoff"}""", pendingInputDescription: "Approve Q3 audit report publication?"); } // Later, when the external signal arrives, resume the run on the backend: await backend.ResumeAsync(runId, resumeInputJson: """{"approved":true}""", cancellationToken); 3. Submitting Runs with Idempotency & Scope Throttling var backend = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IAgentRunBackend>(); var request = new AgentRunRequest( HandlerId: DataProcessingAgentHandler.StableHandlerId, InputJson: """{"dataset": "sales-q3", "action": "audit"}""", IdempotencyKey: "sales-q3-audit-2026", ScopeKey: "tenant-acme", Deadline: DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddMinutes(15), MaxAttempts: 3); AgentRunSubmission submission = await backend.SubmitAsync(request, cancellationToken); if (submission.WasDeduplicated) { Console.WriteLine($"Duplicate request deduplicated. Existing RunId: {submission.RunId}"); } else { Console.WriteLine($"Enqueued new RunId: {submission.RunId}"); } 4. Batch Submission, Reporting & Cancellation MyAgents.Runtime.Workers includes AgentRunBatchSubmitter, AgentRunBatchReporter, and AgentRunBatchController for managing large batches of durable runs: using MyAgents.Core.Execution; using MyAgents.Runtime.Workers; var submitter = new AgentRunBatchSubmitter(backend); var reporter = new AgentRunBatchReporter((IAgentRunBatchCatalog)backend); var controller = new AgentRunBatchController((IAgentRunBatchController)backend); // 1. Stream batch cases into the backend async IAsyncEnumerable<AgentRunBatchCase> GenerateCasesAsync() { yield return new AgentRunBatchCase("case-1", new AgentRunRequest("data-processing", """{"id":1}""")); yield return new AgentRunBatchCase("case-2", new AgentRunRequest("data-processing", """{"id":2}""")); await Task.CompletedTask; } await foreach (var sub in submitter.SubmitAsync("batch-2026-11", GenerateCasesAsync(), cancellationToken)) { Console.WriteLine($"Submitted run {sub.RunId} for batch-2026-11"); } // 2. Query aggregated batch progress and success rate AgentRunBatchSummary summary = await reporter.GetSummaryAsync("batch-2026-11", cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"Total: {summary.RunCount}, Succeeded: {summary.SucceededCount}, Pending: {summary.PendingCount}, Complete: {summary.IsComplete}"); // 3. Cancel remaining runs in the batch if needed int cancelled = await controller.CancelAsync("batch-2026-11", cancellationToken);

docs/getting-started/packages.html.title: Package Ecosystem | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/getting-started/packages.html.summary: Package Ecosystem MyAgents Community is built as a set of modular, decoupled NuGet packages for .NET 10. Install only what your application requires. Core Packages Matrix Package Version Description Target Use Case MyAgents.Core 1.0.0 Core abstractions: IAgent, AgentDefinition, IAgentSession, ITool, messages, and prompts. Included in all applications. MyAgents.Runtime.Chat 1.0.0 Provider-neutral conversational runtime integrating with Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient. Interactive chat applications, CLI bots, web APIs. MyAgents.Generators 1.0.0 Roslyn incremental source generator for [AgentTool] compile-time tool binding. High-performance and NativeAOT trimmed applications. MyAgents.Memory 1.0.0 SIMD dense vector similarity (TensorPrimitives), BM25 sparse index, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, document readers. In-memory RAG, semantic search, long-term memory. MyAgents.Runtime.Workers 1.0.0 Durable background worker host with lease coordination, idempotency, and retries. Long-running asynchronous workflows, background task queues. MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite 1.0.0 SQLite-backed persistent run backend for durable worker execution. On-premises and single-node durable worker storage. MyAgents.Mcp 1.0.0 Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool adapters for stdio and HTTP/SSE transports. Connecting to local or remote MCP servers and tools. MyAgents.Agents 1.0.0 High-level orchestrations: subagents, group chat, token cost tracking, and model routing. Complex multi-agent teams, hierarchical delegation. MyAgents.Testing 1.0.0 In-memory test runtime, deterministic mock agents, and turn assertions. Unit tests and integration test suites. Installation Commands Conversational Chat Agent dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat High-Performance NativeAOT Agent with Compile-Time Tools dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package MyAgents.Generators Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package MyAgents.Memory Durable Worker Process (Background Queue) dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Workers dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite External MCP Tools Integration dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package MyAgents.Mcp Multi-Agent Workflows & Cost Routing dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package MyAgents.Agents Unit Testing Suite dotnet add package MyAgents.Testing

docs/getting-started/quickstart.html.title: Quick Start Guide | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/getting-started/quickstart.html.summary: Quick Start Guide In this guide, you will build and run your first tool-calling AI agent using MyAgents Community in under 5 minutes. Prerequisites .NET 10 SDK An API key for an LLM provider (e.g., OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, or Anthropic) or an in-memory test runtime. 1. Create a New Console Application dotnet new console -n MyFirstAgent cd MyFirstAgent 2. Add Required NuGet Packages Install the core contracts, reusable agent features, chat runtime, and your preferred AI client: dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Agents dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI Note MyAgents Community is completely provider-neutral. It interfaces directly with any Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient implementation (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, GitHub Models, AWS Bedrock, etc.). 3. Build Your First Agent Replace Program.cs with the following code: using System.ComponentModel; using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Prompts; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; using MyAgents.Runtime.Chat; using OpenAI; // 1. Configure the AI Chat Client var apiKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("OPENAI_API_KEY") ?? "your-api-key"; IChatClient chatClient = new OpenAIClient(apiKey) .GetChatClient("gpt-4o-mini") .AsIChatClient(); // 2. Register MyAgents runtime in Dependency Injection var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddSingleton<IChatClient>(chatClient); services.AddMyAgentsChatRuntime(options => { options.DefaultModelId = "gpt-4o-mini"; options.MaxToolRoundTrips = 5; }); await using var serviceProvider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var sessionFactory = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IAgentSessionFactory>(); // 3. Define the Agent and its capabilities using composable features var promptRegistry = new PromptRegistry() .Register(new PromptTemplateDefinition( Name: "system.weather", Version: "1.0", Template: "You are a concise, helpful assistant. Always use tools to answer weather queries.", Description: "Weather assistant system prompt")); var toolsFeature = new ToolsFeature() .AddFunction( ([Description("The city name")] string city) => $"Weather in {city}: 21°C (70°F), Clear Skies", name: "get_weather", description: "Gets the current temperature and conditions for a given city."); var definition = new AgentDefinition("weather-assistant", [ new PromptRegistryFeature(promptRegistry, systemTemplateName: "system.weather"), toolsFeature ]); // 4. Create an isolated conversation session await using var session = sessionFactory.CreateSession("session-demo-1", definition); // 5. Invoke the agent Console.WriteLine("User: What's the weather in Vancouver?"); var result = await session.InvokeAsync([ AgentMessage.FromText("user", "What's the weather in Vancouver?") ]); // 6. Display the assistant's response and turn telemetry foreach (var message in result.Output) { Console.WriteLine($"Assistant: {message.Content}"); } Console.WriteLine($"Tool calls executed: {result.Telemetry.ToolCalls} (Duration: {result.Telemetry.TurnDuration.TotalMilliseconds:F0}ms)"); 4. Run the Application dotnet run Expected Output User: What's the weather in Vancouver? Assistant: The current weather in Vancouver is 21°C (70°F) with clear skies. Tool calls executed: 1 (Duration: 420ms) Authoring a Custom IAgentFeature In addition to built-in features like ToolsFeature and PromptRegistryFeature, you can group related prompts, tools, capabilities, and middleware into a dedicated IAgentFeature: using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; public sealed class UtcClockFeature : IAgentFeature { public void Contribute(AgentAssembly assembly) { assembly.Prompts.AddSystem("Use the get_current_utc_time tool when asked for the current UTC time."); assembly.Tools.Add(DelegateTool.Create( () => DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToString("O"), name: "get_current_utc_time", description: "Returns the current UTC date and time in ISO-8601 format.")); } } Next Steps Explore Package Ecosystem to discover additional modules like RAG, background workers, and source generators. Learn about NativeAOT Tools for compile-time reflection-free performance. Learn about Agent State Graphs and Durable Runs for crash-resilient background processing.

docs/governance/canary-egress-defense.ht.title: Canary Egress Defense | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/governance/canary-egress-defense.ht.summary:
Canary Egress Defense Most agent safety in MyAgents is inbound (IGuardrailPolicy inspects what the model produced) or human oversight (IToolApprovalGate decides whether a tool may run). Neither answers the question an attacker actually cares about: is secret material leaving the process? Canary egress defense answers it. A high-entropy canary token is issued for each session and placed in the system prompt. Every outbound payload — the assistant's reply, the JSON arguments of every tool call, and every durable memory write — is scanned for that token before it leaves. A hit fails closed: the turn is replaced with a uniform refusal and the session is quarantined. flowchart TD Model["Model / IChatClient"] Prompt["System prompt + canary directive"] Prompt --> Model Model -->|"assistant text"| MW["CanaryEgressMiddleware
buffered"] Model -->|"tool call args"| OBS["CanaryToolEgressObserver
before InvokeAsync"] Mem["IMemoryStore.SetAsync"] --> STORE["Guarded memory store"] MW --> Guard["Egress scan
size cap → canary → heuristics"] OBS --> Guard STORE --> Guard Guard -->|"Informational"| Pass["payload proceeds"] Guard -->|"Suspicious / Confirmed"| Handler["ICanaryViolationHandler"] Handler -->|"Allow"| Pass Handler -->|"Abort"| Block["Uniform refusal / CanaryViolationException"] Block --> Quarantine["Session quarantined — monotonic"] Quarantine -.->|"every later turn refused"| MW Getting started Enable the feature on the agent definition. Everything else is opt-in configuration: using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Agents; var agent = new AgentDefinition( "GuardedAgent", Features: [ new ToolsFeature(/* ... */), new CanaryDefenseFeature(), ]); To record violations for tuning, and to allow a CDN in markdown images: var auditSink = new InMemoryEgressAuditSink(); var feature = new CanaryDefenseFeature(options => { options.AuditSink = auditSink; // record every finding options.BeaconHostAllowList = ["cdn.example.com"]; // markdown images from here are fine options.SecretPatterns = [ new SecretPattern("aws-access-key", new Regex(@"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}", RegexOptions.Compiled)), ]; }); Scanned channels EgressChannel names the three outbound paths that are checked. Channel Interception point Possible reactions TurnOutput CanaryEgressMiddleware, after the turn and before it is yielded replace with the uniform refusal, or allow ToolArguments CanaryToolEgressObserver, before ITool.InvokeAsync abort the call, or allow MemoryWrite guarded IMemoryStore.SetAsync decorator, before persisting abort the write, or allow Arguments and memory writes cannot be rewritten — the observer contract returns no value and the runtime passes the original argument string to the tool. On those channels the only outcomes are abort or allow. Redaction is not available. What is detected The session canary, matched exactly. Obfuscated canaries — zero-width characters stripped, the payload reversed, and Base64 / hex / percent-encoded runs decoded, then re-matched. Fragmented canaries across turns — a bounded window of recent turn output is scanned with the current turn, and a pass that ignores interleaved prose reassembles fragments. Markdown image beacons — an image pointing at a host outside BeaconHostAllowList. Images are auto-fetched by most chat surfaces, so the URL is a silent one-way channel. High-entropy URLs — a query string that looks like a payload. SecretPatterns — opt-in named regular expressions. A match reports the pattern's Name and never logs the matched secret. Findings carry an EgressSeverity: Informational, Suspicious (heuristics, may be a false positive) or Confirmed (a canary, or a payload over the scan cap). Reactions Reaction is decided by an ICanaryViolationHandler, not by options. Handler Confirmed Suspicious QuarantineSessionViolationHandler (default) quarantines the session and aborts audited, turn continues AuditOnlyViolationHandler allowed allowed AuditOnlyViolationHandler exists for shadow-mode rollout: measure trigger rates on real traffic before enforcing. It lets confirmed canaries through by design — do not ship it to production. A blocked turn produces exactly one message and a blocked tool call throws CanaryViolationException, whose Message is the uniform string "The turn was aborted by egress defense.". The refusal the caller sees is "I'm sorry, but I cannot provide a response to that request." — the same text guardrails use, so a caller cannot tell which control fired. Detail is kept in Reason, which is for host diagnostics and audit logs only. Never surface Reason to the model: naming the detector hands an attacker the feedback needed to iterate until a payload gets through. CanaryViolationException implements INonRetryableException, so ResilienceMiddleware will not retry it even under a classifier that reports every exception as transient. Quarantine is monotonic: once a session is quarantined, nothing clears it, and later turns are refused without spending a model call. Audit trail The meter records aggregate counts. IEgressAuditSink records the individual events, which is what threshold tuning needs: public sealed record EgressAuditRecord( string AuditId, string SessionId, EgressChannel Channel, EgressSeverity Severity, string DetectorName, string Reason, DateTimeOffset Timestamp, string? ToolName = null); IEgressAuditSink exposes RecordAsync, ListBySessionAsync and ListAllAsync. InMemoryEgressAuditSink is the supplied implementation; the interface is the extension point for a durable sink. A sink that throws does not fail the turn — losing an audit record must not take the agent down. Options reference Option Default Meaning AuditSink null IEgressAuditSink receiving one record per finding MaxScanBytes 1 MiB Payloads over this are rejected unscanned FailOpenOnScannerError false When true, a throwing IEgressScanner is ignored instead of blocking BeaconHostAllowList empty Hosts permitted in markdown image URLs; empty flags every image SecretPatterns empty Opt-in SecretPattern list ScanToolArguments true Scan tool-call arguments before the tool runs ScanMemoryWrites true Scan IMemoryStore.SetAsync payloads before persisting States, and what happens in each State Behaviour Empty payload Clean. An empty turn is not a failure. Over the scan cap Rejected without scanning; failing closed, because truncating would let a canary sit just past the cut. Scanner throws Blocks by default; FailOpenOnScannerError opts into ignoring it. Already quarantined Every later turn is refused before the model is called; tool calls and memory writes throw. Concurrent turns Canary reads are lock-free; the first quarantine wins and is idempotent. Limits Read these before relying on the feature in production. Detection is not prevention. An attacker can still leak information one bit per turn through a signal that never touches a scanned payload. This raises the cost of exfiltration; it does not close the channel. Cross-turn coverage is bounded: the window retains 8 turns and 8 KiB. A split spanning more than 8 turns, or whose fragments exceed that budget, is not caught. Both bounds are internal constants, not options. Fragment matching is order-preserving, so interleaving canary-alphabet characters between fragments defeats it. MemoryWrite guards only the decorated store. Code that holds an IMemoryStore obtained outside the session bypasses the decorator. Streaming is buffered for any agent using this feature: a canary can appear in the final tokens of a reply, and text already yielded cannot be retracted. Thresholds are untuned defaults — 1 MiB scan cap, 8-turn / 8 KiB window, entropy ≥ 4.0 bits per character. Measure before enforcing. Canary survival depends on the provider. A provider that truncates or summarises long system prompts may drop the canary, and then nothing trips. Verify against your provider before relying on enforcement. Use this alongside least-privilege tools and human approval, not instead of them. API surface MyAgents.Core.Security: EgressChannel, EgressSeverity, EgressFinding, EgressScanResult IEgressScanner — pluggable heuristics; canaries are matched by the framework ICanaryVault — the session's canaries and its quarantine state ICanaryViolationHandler, CanaryDisposition, CanaryViolationContext, CanaryViolationException IEgressAuditSink, EgressAuditRecord, InMemoryEgressAuditSink SecretPattern MyAgents.Core: INonRetryableException — implemented by CanaryViolationException MyAgents.Agents: CanaryDefenseFeature, CanaryDefenseOptions QuarantineSessionViolationHandler, AuditOnlyViolationHandler The design rationale, verified platform constraints and risk register live in design/0001-canary-egress-defense.md in the repository.

docs/governance/circuit-breakers.html.title: Circuit Breakers, Tool Observers & OpenTelemetry | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/governance/circuit-breakers.html.summary: Circuit Breakers, Tool Observers & OpenTelemetry To protect downstream dependencies from cascading failures and give operators full visibility into agent behavior, MyAgents Community provides circuit breaker middleware, tool call observers, and first-class OpenTelemetry tracing and metrics. 1. Circuit Breaker Middleware (CircuitBreakerMiddleware) When an LLM provider or downstream dependency experiences transient failures (such as HTTP 429/503 errors or timeouts), CircuitBreakerMiddleware tracks consecutive transient failures via ITransientErrorClassifier and trips open (CircuitState.Open), fast-failing with CircuitBreakerOpenException until OpenDuration elapses: using MyAgents.Core; var circuitBreaker = new CircuitBreakerMiddleware( failureThreshold: 3, openDuration: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30), classifier: new DefaultTransientErrorClassifier()); // Inspect state (Closed, Open, HalfOpen) or manually reset Console.WriteLine($"Circuit state: {circuitBreaker.State}"); circuitBreaker.Reset(); Register CircuitBreakerMiddleware in an agent's pipeline using a custom feature or assembly.Pipeline.Use(circuitBreaker). 2. Tool Call Observers (IToolCallObserver) IToolCallObserver lets you log, audit, or time every tool execution without modifying the tool implementation itself: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging; using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; public sealed class SecurityAuditToolObserver : IToolCallObserver { private readonly ILogger _logger; public SecurityAuditToolObserver(ILogger logger) { _logger = logger; } public ValueTask OnToolCallingAsync( ToolCallObservation call, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { _logger.LogInformation( "Session {SessionId} invoking tool {ToolName} (CallId: {CallId}) with args: {Args}", call.SessionId, call.ToolName, call.CallId, call.Arguments); return ValueTask.CompletedTask; } public ValueTask OnToolCalledAsync( ToolResultObservation result, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { _logger.LogInformation( "Tool {ToolName} finished in {ElapsedMs:F1}ms (Failed: {HasError})", result.Call.ToolName, result.Duration.TotalMilliseconds, result.Exception is not null); return ValueTask.CompletedTask; } } Attach one or more observers to an AgentDefinition via ToolObserverFeature: var definition = new AgentDefinition("audited-agent", [ new ToolObserverFeature(new SecurityAuditToolObserver(logger)), new ToolsFeature(myTool) ]); 3. OpenTelemetry Tracing & Metrics (MyAgentsOtelExtensions) MyAgents.Core (MyAgentsTelemetry) and MyAgents.Agents (TelemetryFeature, MyAgentsOtelExtensions) integrate directly with System.Diagnostics.ActivitySource, System.Diagnostics.Metrics.Meter, and .NET Aspire: Enabling Telemetry on an Agent Add TelemetryFeature (and optionally LoggingFeature) to your AgentDefinition: using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; var definition = new AgentDefinition("observable-agent", [ new TelemetryFeature(), new LoggingFeature(), new ToolsFeature(myTool) ]); Registering OpenTelemetry in Program.cs Use the AddMyAgentsTracing() and AddMyAgentsMetrics() extension methods on OpenTelemetryBuilder: using MyAgents.Agents; using OpenTelemetry.Metrics; using OpenTelemetry.Trace; builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry() .AddMyAgentsTracing() // Subscribes to "MyAgents" and "Microsoft.Extensions.AI" ActivitySources .AddMyAgentsMetrics() // Subscribes to the "MyAgents" Meter .WithTracing(tracing => tracing.AddOtlpExporter()) .WithMetrics(metrics => metrics.AddOtlpExporter()); Exported instrumentation includes: Activity Source (MyAgents & Microsoft.Extensions.AI): End-to-end distributed spans across agent turns, middleware, LLM provider calls, and tool executions. Metrics (MyAgents): agent.turn.duration_ms: Histogram of conversational turn durations. agent.turn.tokens: Token usage counters (prompt, completion, total). agent.turn.errors: Counter of turn exceptions and failures.

docs/governance/guardrails-and-resilienc.title: Guardrails, Retries, Fallbacks & Dead-Letter Queues | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/governance/guardrails-and-resilienc.summary: Guardrails, Retries, Fallbacks & Dead-Letter Queues Production AI systems must validate model outputs before they reach users and recover gracefully from transient provider outages or unhandled exceptions. MyAgents Community provides a layered defense pipeline via GuardrailsFeature, ResilienceMiddleware, and FallbackFeature. Defense-in-Depth Pipeline Ordering When composing resilience and safety features on an AgentDefinition, order them from outermost to innermost: flowchart LR Caller["Caller"] --> Fallback["1. FallbackFeature (Outermost)"] Fallback --> Resilience["2. ResilienceMiddleware (Retries)"] Resilience --> Circuit["3. CircuitBreakerMiddleware"] Circuit --> Guardrails["4. GuardrailsFeature (Output Validation)"] Guardrails --> Runtime["ChatClientRuntime (IChatClient)"] 1. Content-Safety Output Guardrails (GuardrailsFeature) GuardrailsFeature attaches GuardrailMiddleware to evaluate every turn's output against an ordered list of IGuardrailPolicy implementations. If any policy returns a GuardrailViolation, the violating output is replaced outright with violation.ReplacementMessage (never leaking partial violating content, even on streaming calls). Built-in Guardrail Policies EmptyResponseGuardrailPolicy: Flags turns whose output is empty or whitespace-only (enabled by default in new GuardrailsFeature()). MaxLengthGuardrailPolicy(maxLength): Flags turns whose total character length exceeds maxLength. BlocklistGuardrailPolicy(blockedPhrases): Case-insensitive substring check against prohibited phrases, secrets, or competitor names. using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; var definition = new AgentDefinition("customer-facing-agent", [ new GuardrailsFeature( new EmptyResponseGuardrailPolicy(), new MaxLengthGuardrailPolicy(maxLength: 4000), new BlocklistGuardrailPolicy(["INTERNAL_ONLY", "CONFIDENTIAL_PROJECT_X"])) ]); Custom IGuardrailPolicy Implement IGuardrailPolicy for custom PII redaction, regex validation, or moderation checks: using MyAgents.Core; public sealed class NoCreditCardGuardrailPolicy : IGuardrailPolicy { public ValueTask<GuardrailViolation?> EvaluateAsync( IReadOnlyList<AgentMessage> output, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { foreach (var message in output) { if (message.Content is not null && message.Content.Contains("4111-", StringComparison.Ordinal)) { return ValueTask.FromResult<GuardrailViolation?>(new GuardrailViolation( PolicyName: nameof(NoCreditCardGuardrailPolicy), Reason: "Output contained a masked or raw payment card pattern.", ReplacementMessage: "I cannot display payment card numbers.")); } } return ValueTask.FromResult<GuardrailViolation?>(null); } } 2. Transient Retry Middleware (ResilienceMiddleware) ResilienceMiddleware uses ITransientErrorClassifier (DefaultTransientErrorClassifier) to retry transient network or HTTP rate-limit failures with exponential backoff: using MyAgents.Core; var resilience = new ResilienceMiddleware( classifier: new DefaultTransientErrorClassifier(), maxRetries: 3, baseDelay: TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500)); 3. Graceful Fallbacks & Dead-Letter Queues (FallbackFeature) When all retries are exhausted or an unrecoverable exception occurs, FallbackFeature (FallbackMiddleware) catches the exception and invokes an IFallbackPolicy so the caller receives a controlled response while failed turns are captured for inspection: Static Fallback (StaticFallbackPolicy) using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; var fallback = new FallbackFeature( new StaticFallbackPolicy("The assistant is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.")); Dead-Letter Queue Capture (DeadLetterFallbackPolicy) Use DeadLetterFallbackPolicy with IDeadLetterQueue (InMemoryDeadLetterQueue or your own persistent queue) to record failed turn messages, session IDs, timestamps, and exceptions for alerting or replay: using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; var deadLetterQueue = new InMemoryDeadLetterQueue(); var definition = new AgentDefinition("resilient-support-agent", [ new FallbackFeature(new DeadLetterFallbackPolicy( queue: deadLetterQueue, fallbackMessage: "We recorded your request and an engineer will follow up.")), new GuardrailsFeature() ]); // Inspect captured dead letters for alerting or replay foreach (DeadLetter item in deadLetterQueue.Items) { Console.WriteLine($"Failed session {item.SessionId} at {item.FailedAt:O}: {item.Exception.Message}"); }

docs/governance/tool-approval.html.title: Tool Approval, Gates & Audit Trails | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/governance/tool-approval.html.summary: Tool Approval, Gates & Audit Trails When AI agents execute tools that mutate production state, run shell commands, or call external APIs, granular governance is essential. MyAgents Community provides a multi-stage tool approval pipeline built into MyAgents.Core. The Tool Approval Pipeline Every tool call requested by a model is evaluated by ToolApprovalEvaluator before the tool handler runs: flowchart LR Model["Model Requests Tool Call"] --> Memory["1. ISessionApprovalMemory"] Memory -->|No Cached Grant| Policy["2. IToolApprovalPolicy"] Policy -->|Approved| Audit["4. IToolApprovalAuditSink"] Policy -->|Pending| Gate["3. IToolApprovalGate"] Policy -->|Rejected| Reject["Return Rejection to Model"] Gate -->|Approved / Rejected| Store["IToolApprovalStore & Session Memory"] Store --> Audit Audit --> Exec["Execute ITool.InvokeAsync"] 1. Rule-Based Approval Policies (RuleBasedToolApprovalPolicy) Configure allowlists, denylists, regex argument rules, and human-approval requirements using RuleBasedToolApprovalPolicy: using System.Text.RegularExpressions; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Core; var policy = new RuleBasedToolApprovalPolicy() // 1. Safe read-only tools execute automatically .AllowTool("get_current_utc_time", reason: "Read-only clock tool") .AllowTool("search_knowledge_base", reason: "Read-only RAG search") // 2. Block dangerous arguments using regex inspection .AddArgumentPatternRule( toolPattern: "execute_sql", argumentRegex: new Regex(@"\b(DROP|DELETE|TRUNCATE|ALTER)\b", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase), decision: ToolApprovalDecision.Reject(decidedBy: "security-policy", reason: "Destructive SQL is prohibited.")) // 3. Sensitive tools pause for interactive gate approval (returns ToolApprovalStatus.Pending) .RequireApprovalForTool("deploy_production", reason: "Production deployment requires operator sign-off") // 4. Custom predicate rule .AddRule(request => request.ToolName.StartsWith("internal_", StringComparison.Ordinal) ? ToolApprovalDecision.Reject("policy", "Internal tools are disabled.") : null) // 5. Reject any other unknown tool by default .SetDefaultDecision(ToolApprovalDecision.Reject( decidedBy: "default-policy", reason: "Tool is not in the approved allowlist.")); services.AddSingleton<IToolApprovalPolicy>(policy); Other built-in policies include: AllowAllToolApprovalPolicy: Approves all tool calls (default when no policy is registered). RequireApprovalPolicy: Marks every tool call as Pending so an IToolApprovalGate is always consulted. 2. Human-in-the-Loop Approval Gates (IToolApprovalGate) When a policy returns ToolApprovalStatus.Pending, ToolApprovalEvaluator invokes the registered IToolApprovalGate (EvaluateOrPromptAsync): Built-in Gates ConsolePromptApprovalGate: Interactive CLI prompt for console applications. services.AddSingleton<IToolApprovalGate>( new ConsolePromptApprovalGate(Console.In, Console.Out, autoApproveNonInteractive: false)); CallbackToolApprovalGate: Delegate-based gate for custom webhooks or UI dialogs. var gate = new CallbackToolApprovalGate(async (request, pendingDecision, ct) => { bool approved = await mySlackNotifier.AskSupervisorAsync(request.ToolName, request.ArgumentsJson, ct); return approved ? ToolApprovalDecision.Approve( decidedBy: "supervisor@acme.com", reason: "Approved via Slack", scope: ApprovalScope.SessionTool) : ToolApprovalDecision.Reject( decidedBy: "supervisor@acme.com", reason: "Denied via Slack"); }); services.AddSingleton<IToolApprovalGate>(gate); AsyncSignalApprovalGate: Asynchronous signal queue where external HTTP endpoints can inspect gate.PendingRequests and complete decisions via gate.TrySubmitDecision(approvalId, decision). 3. Session Approval Scopes & Audit Sinks When approving a tool call, you can specify an ApprovalScope so the human operator is not prompted repeatedly during the same session: ApprovalScope.Once: Valid only for this single tool invocation. ApprovalScope.SessionCall: Remembers approval for the same tool and identical JSON arguments within the session. ApprovalScope.SessionTool: Remembers approval for all future calls to the same tool within the session. ApprovalScope.SessionAlways: Approves all subsequent tool calls in the session. Register ISessionApprovalMemory, IToolApprovalStore, and IToolApprovalAuditSink in DI to persist and inspect decisions: var sessionMemory = new InMemorySessionApprovalMemory(); var approvalStore = new InMemoryToolApprovalStore(); var auditSink = new InMemoryToolApprovalAuditSink(); services.AddSingleton<ISessionApprovalMemory>(sessionMemory); services.AddSingleton<IToolApprovalStore>(approvalStore); services.AddSingleton<IToolApprovalAuditSink>(auditSink); // After running turns, inspect the immutable audit log: IReadOnlyList<ToolApprovalAuditRecord> auditRecords = await auditSink.ListAllAsync(); foreach (var record in auditRecords) { Console.WriteLine($"{record.Timestamp:O} | {record.ToolName} | {record.Decision.Status} by {record.Decision.DecidedBy} ({record.GateType})"); }

docs/index.html.title: Documentation Guides | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/index.html.summary: Documentation Guides Welcome to the MyAgents Community documentation. Explore guides, architectural patterns, and code samples across the entire platform. 🚀 Getting Started Quick Start: Build and run your first tool-calling AI agent in under 5 minutes. Package Ecosystem: Explore the 9 modular packages for .NET 10. 🏗️ Core Concepts Architecture & Execution Lifecycle: Understand how session factories, feature pipelines, and turn loops interact with IChatClient. Sessions & Turns: Manage isolated conversation state, streaming responses, and context windows. Structured Output & Multi-Modal: Enforce JSON schemas with automatic self-correction retries and send image, audio, video, or document inputs. Prompt Registry & Templates: Manage versioned system prompt templates with variable interpolation. ⚡ Tools & Extensibility NativeAOT Tools: Generate zero-reflection, compile-time tools using MyAgents.Generators. Delegate & Custom Tools: Create tools from in-process C# lambdas, ToolsFeature, WebSearchFeature, or custom ITool classes. Model Context Protocol (MCP): Connect your agent to external tools, prompts, and resources over stdio or HTTP/SSE with dynamic hot-reload and skill discovery. 🔀 Workflows & State Graphs Agent State Graphs: Build cyclic or DAG workflows with AgentGraph<TState>, conditional routing, parallel fan-out, SendPacket<TState> map-reduce, and snapshot time-travel. Checkpointed Workflows & HITL: Pause and resume stateful IWorkflow<TState> pipelines across process restarts for human input or tool approvals. Orchestration Patterns: Execute iterative AgentLoop reductions, planner-worker-synthesizer plans (OrchestratorSteps), generator-critic loops (ReflectionSteps), majority-vote ConsensusSteps, and adaptive goal prioritization. 🛡️ Durable Execution & Resilience Durable Agent Runs & Batches: Host crash-resilient, restart-recoverable workloads using SQLite leases, admission throttling, batch controllers, and background worker services. 🔍 Memory & Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Hybrid RAG & Vector Stores: Fuse dense SIMD cosine similarity (TensorPrimitives.Dot) with BM25 sparse lexical ranking across in-memory, SQLite, and Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData stores. Document Ingestion & Chunking: Ingest and chunk Markdown, HTML, Plain Text, and JSON with zero third-party dependencies, content-hash deduplication, and agentic knowledge base tools. Episodic Memory: Enable cross-session recall, automated episode consolidation, and retention policies. 🔒 Governance, Guardrails & Observability Tool Approval & Allowlisting: Enforce rule-based permission policies, session approval memory, audit sinks, and human-in-the-loop approval gates. Guardrails, Fallbacks & Resilience: Protect agent outputs with GuardrailsFeature, retry transient provider errors with ResilienceMiddleware, and capture failures with FallbackFeature and dead-letter queues. Circuit Breakers & Observability: Protect against cascade failures, monitor tool invocations with IToolCallObserver, and emit OpenTelemetry traces and metrics (AddMyAgentsTracing, AddMyAgentsMetrics). 👥 Multi-Agent Systems & Testing Subagents, Group Chats & Routing: Orchestrate hierarchical subagent dispatching, GroupChat / SelectorGroupChat, CapabilityRouter, and multi-model token cost routing. Unit Testing Agents: Write fast, deterministic unit tests using MyAgents.Testing (InMemoryAgent, FakeAgentSession, InMemoryAgentRuntime, InMemoryAgentRunBackend).

docs/memory/document-ingestion.html.title: Document Ingestion, Chunking & Knowledge Base Tools | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/memory/document-ingestion.html.summary: Document Ingestion, Chunking & Knowledge Base Tools The MyAgents.Memory package includes a complete document ingestion pipeline with zero third-party parsing dependencies, boundary-aware chunkers, atomic source replacement, and agentic knowledge base tools. Supported Document Formats (IDocumentReader) CompositeDocumentReader and HtmlDocumentReader extract clean text and document titles directly from streams or files: Markdown (.md, text/markdown): Extracts YAML front-matter title: or the first # H1 heading and preserves heading hierarchy and fenced code blocks. HTML (.html, .htm, text/html): Extracts <title> or <h1>, strips <script> / <style> / <nav> boilerplate, converts headings/lists/code/links into structured Markdown, and decodes HTML entities. Plain Text (.txt, text/plain): Reads UTF-8 text with paragraph and sentence-boundary chunking. JSON (.json, application/json): Formats and extracts structured JSON content. 1. Configuring Document Ingestion in DI Use AddDocumentIngestion to register IDocumentIngestor, IDocumentReader, ITextChunker, ITokenCounter, and KnowledgeBaseFeature: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Memory; var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddSqliteMemoryStore("knowledge.db"); services.AddDocumentIngestion(builder => { // Configure chunk size, overlap, and optional token budget per chunk builder.WithChunkingOptions(new TextChunkingOptions( ChunkSize: 1000, ChunkOverlap: 150, MaxTokens: 256)); // Use heading-aware Markdown chunker (prepends "# H1 > ## H2" breadcrumbs to chunks) builder.UseMarkdownChunker(includeHeadingBreadcrumbs: true); // Use zero-allocation approximate token counter (or register a custom ITokenCounter) builder.UseTokenCounter(ApproximateTokenCounter.Instance); }); await using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var ingestor = provider.GetRequiredService<IDocumentIngestor>(); 2. Ingesting Files, Streams, and Batches Ingest a Local File (IngestFileAsync) DocumentIngestionResult fileResult = await ingestor.IngestFileAsync( ns: "project-docs", filePath: "docs/architecture.md", source: "docs/architecture.md", metadata: new Dictionary<string, string> { ["version"] = "1.0.0", ["team"] = "platform" }, cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"Ingested '{fileResult.Source}' into {fileResult.Chunks.Count} chunks (replaced {fileResult.ReplacedChunkCount} prior chunks)."); Ingest a Stream (IngestStreamAsync) await using var htmlStream = File.OpenRead("release-notes.html"); DocumentIngestionResult streamResult = await ingestor.IngestStreamAsync( ns: "project-docs", content: htmlStream, source: "https://example.com/release-notes", contentTypeOrExtension: "text/html", cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Batch Ingestion & Atomic Source Replacement (IngestBatchAsync) Re-ingesting a document with the same Source automatically removes stale chunks, reuses embeddings for unchanged chunks (via SHA-256 content hashes), and updates the BM25Index: BatchDocumentIngestionResult batchResult = await ingestor.IngestBatchAsync( ns: "project-docs", documents: [ new IngestDocument(Source: "guide-1", Content: "# Intro\nWelcome to MyAgents.", Title: "Intro Guide"), new IngestDocument(Source: "guide-2", Content: "# Security\nAlways configure tool policies.", Title: "Security Guide") ], cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"Total chunks: {batchResult.TotalChunks}, Replaced: {batchResult.TotalReplacedChunks}"); // Delete all chunks for a document source int deletedChunks = await ingestor.DeleteDocumentAsync("project-docs", source: "guide-1", cancellationToken); 3. Agentic Knowledge Base Tools (KnowledgeBaseFeature) In addition to passive middleware injection (RetrievalAugmentationFeature), you can give an agent active tools to search and ingest documents on demand using KnowledgeBaseFeature: search_knowledge_base: Executes a hybrid semantic + BM25 search with optional source filtering and returns numbered citations with provenance metadata. ingest_knowledge_document: Chunks, embeds, and indexes a document into the knowledge base namespace. using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Memory; var kbFeature = provider.GetRequiredService<KnowledgeBaseFeature>(); var definition = new AgentDefinition("knowledge-curator", [ kbFeature ]);

docs/memory/episodic-memory.html.title: Episodic Memory & Retention Policies | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/memory/episodic-memory.html.summary: Episodic Memory & Retention Policies While standard session state is tied to a single conversation, real-world agents require long-term episodic memory to remember user preferences, architectural decisions, and domain milestones across separate sessions and days. What is Episodic Memory? MyAgents.Memory provides IEpisodicMemoryStore (EpisodicMemoryStore), a structured long-term memory layer built on top of IMemoryStore and IHybridMemoryRetriever: Structured Episodes (EpisodicMemoryEntry): Stores EpisodeId, SessionId, Summary, KeyFacts, Entities, Timestamp, and Salience (0.0 to 1.0). Cross-Session Hybrid Recall (RecallEpisodesAsync): Searches past episodes using hybrid semantic + BM25 retrieval with optional session, age, and minimum salience filters. Episode Consolidation (ConsolidateEpisodesAsync): Merges older, lower-salience episodes for a session into consolidated milestone entries. Retention & Summarization (MemoryRetentionService): Enforces entry count and age limits while optionally summarizing trimmed entries and updating the BM25 lexical index. 1. Setting up Episodic Memory using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Core.Memory; using MyAgents.Memory; var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddSingleton<IMemoryStore, InMemoryMemoryStore>(); // Registers IEpisodicMemoryStore, HybridMemoryRetriever, and EpisodicMemoryFeature services.AddEpisodicMemory(ns: "user-longterm-memory"); await using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var episodicStore = provider.GetRequiredService<IEpisodicMemoryStore>(); 2. Saving, Recalling & Consolidating Episodes Programmatically // 1. Save an episode var episode = new EpisodicMemoryEntry( EpisodeId: "ep-001", SessionId: "session-42", Summary: "User prefers NativeAOT deployments on Linux containers with SQLite WAL persistence.", KeyFacts: ["Target runtime: .NET 10 NativeAOT", "Database: SQLite WAL mode"], Entities: ["NativeAOT", "SQLite"], Timestamp: DateTimeOffset.UtcNow, Salience: 0.95); await episodicStore.SaveEpisodeAsync(episode, cancellationToken); // 2. Recall episodes across sessions var query = new EpisodicRecallQuery( Query: "deployment database preference", SessionIdFilter: null, MaxEpisodes: 5, MinSalience: 0.5, MaxAge: TimeSpan.FromDays(90)); IReadOnlyList<EpisodicMemoryEntry> recalled = await episodicStore.RecallEpisodesAsync(query, cancellationToken); // 3. Consolidate older episodes for a session into a single milestone await episodicStore.ConsolidateEpisodesAsync( sessionId: "session-42", olderThan: TimeSpan.FromDays(7), cancellationToken: cancellationToken); 3. Equipping an Agent with Episodic Memory Tools (EpisodicMemoryFeature) Register EpisodicMemoryFeature on an AgentDefinition to give the model autonomous tools to record and search episodic memories: var episodicFeature = provider.GetRequiredService<EpisodicMemoryFeature>(); var definition = new AgentDefinition("personal-architect", [ episodicFeature ]); EpisodicMemoryFeature registers two tools: save_episodic_fact: Persists an important user fact, preference, or milestone summary (session_id, summary, key_facts, entities, salience). recall_past_episodes: Searches long-term episodic memory for relevant past conversations (query, session_id, max_episodes). 4. Memory Retention Policies (MemoryRetentionService) Use MemoryRetentionService to prune expired or excess memory entries while optionally generating milestone summaries via IMemorySummaryGenerator: var retentionService = provider.GetRequiredService<MemoryRetentionService>(); var policy = new MemoryRetentionPolicy( MaxEntries: 500, MaxAge: TimeSpan.FromDays(90), SummarizeTrimmedEntries: true, SummaryKeyPrefix: "milestone-summary", SummarySourceCount: 20); MemoryRetentionResult result = await retentionService.ApplyAsync( ns: "user-longterm-memory", policy: policy, cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"Pruned {result.DeletedCount} entries, summarized {result.SummarizedCount} entries.");

docs/memory/hybrid-rag.html.title: Hybrid RAG & Vector Memory Stores | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/memory/hybrid-rag.html.summary: Hybrid RAG & Vector Memory Stores MyAgents.Memory delivers an enterprise-grade retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and memory system with zero mandatory external database dependencies, while also supporting persistent SQLite storage and Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData providers. Why Hybrid Retrieval? Pure vector search (dense embeddings) excels at semantic similarity and conceptual queries, but can miss exact product SKUs, error codes, C# type names, or rare identifiers. Pure keyword search (BM25) excels at exact token matching but lacks semantic understanding. MyAgents Community combines both using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) or Weighted Linear Combination: flowchart TD Query["User Query: 'NativeAOT source generator MYAG001'"] --> Dense["Dense Vector Search (IVectorMemoryStore)"] Query --> Sparse["BM25 Lexical Search (BM25Index)"] Dense -->|"Pre-normalized TensorPrimitives.Dot SIMD"| DenseRanks["Dense Ranked List"] Sparse -->|"Zero-Regex Span Tokenization + TF-IDF"| SparseRanks["Sparse Ranked List"] DenseRanks --> RRF["Reciprocal Rank Fusion / Linear Combination"] SparseRanks --> RRF RRF --> FusedResults["Fused Grounded Context & Citations"] 1. Choosing a Memory Store MyAgents.Memory ships with three IVectorMemoryStore implementations that all support IMemoryStoreChangeNotifier (automatically keeping the BM25Index synchronized on writes and deletes) and SHA-256 content-hash deduplication: Option A: Durable SQLite Vector Store (SqliteMemoryStore) Persists entries, JSON metadata, and binary float embeddings in WAL-mode SQLite while executing SIMD TensorPrimitives.Dot similarity in memory: using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Memory; var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddSingleton<IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>>(embeddingGenerator); // Registers SqliteMemoryStore as IMemoryStore + IVectorMemoryStore and adds HybridMemoryRetriever services.AddSqliteMemoryStore("knowledge.db"); Option B: In-Memory SIMD Vector Store with Snapshots (VectorMemoryStore) High-speed in-memory vector store with binary stream/file snapshot persistence: var vectorStore = new VectorMemoryStore(embeddingGenerator); // Save and restore binary snapshots for fast warm starts await vectorStore.SaveToFileAsync("vectors.snapshot", cancellationToken); int loadedCount = await vectorStore.LoadFromFileAsync("vectors.snapshot", cancellationToken); Option C: Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData Bridge (VectorDataMemoryStore) Bridges any VectorStoreCollection<string, VectorDataMemoryRecord> from the Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData ecosystem: services.AddVectorDataMemoryStore(vectorStoreCollection); Content-Hash Embedding Caching (CachingEmbeddingGenerator) Wrap any IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>> in CachingEmbeddingGenerator to avoid re-computing embeddings for repeated queries or unchanged chunks: var cachedEmbedder = new CachingEmbeddingGenerator(innerEmbeddingGenerator, maxCacheEntries: 4096); Console.WriteLine($"Cache Hits: {cachedEmbedder.CacheHits}, Misses: {cachedEmbedder.CacheMisses}"); 2. Executing a Hybrid Search Query var retriever = provider.GetRequiredService<IHybridMemoryRetriever>(); var query = new HybridMemoryQuery( QueryText: "NativeAOT source generator", MaxResults: 5, DenseWeight: 0.5, SparseWeight: 0.5, RrfK: 60, RankingMode: HybridRankingMode.ReciprocalRankFusion, MinScore: 0.0, MetadataFilters: new Dictionary<string, string> { ["category"] = "tools" }); IReadOnlyList<HybridMemorySearchResult> results = await retriever.SearchHybridAsync( ns: "technical-docs", query: query, cancellationToken: cancellationToken); foreach (var hit in results) { Console.WriteLine($"[Fused: {hit.FusedScore:F4} | DenseRank: {hit.DenseRank} | SparseRank: {hit.SparseRank}] {hit.Entry.Key}"); } 3. Automatic Context Injection & Grounded Citations (RetrievalAugmentationFeature) Register RetrievalAugmentationFeature on an agent to automatically retrieve relevant chunks before each turn, expand adjacent neighbor chunks, enforce token budgets, and verify citation grounding ([1], [2]) on the assistant's response: using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Memory; var ragOptions = new RetrievalAugmentationOptions( Namespace: "technical-docs", MaxResults: 5, MinScore: 0.1, MaxContextTokens: 2000, DeduplicateAcrossTurns: true, AdjacentChunkWindow: 1, AppendCitationReferences: true, OnCitationsEvaluated: grounding => { Console.WriteLine($"Grounded: {grounding.IsGrounded}, Cited sources: {grounding.CitedSources.Count}"); }); var definition = new AgentDefinition("grounded-assistant", [ new RetrievalAugmentationFeature(ragOptions) ]); When AppendCitationReferences: true is enabled and the model cites [1] in its answer, RetrievalAugmentationFeature automatically appends a formatted References: footer with the document title and source provenance.

docs/testing/testing-agents.html.title: Unit Testing Agents, Sessions & Durable Runs | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/testing/testing-agents.html.summary: Unit Testing Agents, Sessions & Durable Runs Testing conversational AI applications against live LLM endpoints is slow, nondeterministic, and expensive. The MyAgents.Testing package provides deterministic, in-memory test doubles for agents, sessions, middleware pipelines, and durable run backends. Installation dotnet add package MyAgents.Testing 1. Testing Agents with InMemoryAgent InMemoryAgent implements IAgent with a FIFO queue of scripted responses and records every AgentTurnContext it receives: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; [TestFixture] public sealed class AgentTests { [Test] public async Task InMemoryAgent_Returns_Queued_Responses_In_Order() { // 1. Arrange a deterministic agent with queued responses and token counts using var agent = new InMemoryAgent("MockReviewer") .EnqueueResponse("Step 1: Static analysis passed.", promptTokens: 40, completionTokens: 12) .EnqueueResponse("Step 2: Ready to merge.", promptTokens: 55, completionTokens: 8) .WithFallbackResponse("Default fallback response"); var services = new AgentTurnServices(new ServiceCollection().BuildServiceProvider()); var context1 = new AgentTurnContext("session-1", [AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Check PR #42")], services); var context2 = new AgentTurnContext("session-1", [AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Approve?")], services); // 2. Act var result1 = await agent.InvokeAsync(context1); var result2 = await agent.InvokeAsync(context2); // 3. Assert Assert.That(result1.Output[0].Content, Is.EqualTo("Step 1: Static analysis passed.")); Assert.That(result1.Telemetry.TotalTokens, Is.EqualTo(52)); Assert.That(result2.Output[0].Content, Is.EqualTo("Step 2: Ready to merge.")); Assert.That(agent.InvocationCount, Is.EqualTo(2)); Assert.That(agent.ReceivedContexts, Has.Count.EqualTo(2)); } } 2. Testing Middleware Pipelines with FakeAgentSession FakeAgentSession wraps an InMemoryAgent inside an IAgentSession so you can unit-test middleware (CircuitBreakerMiddleware, ContextWindowMiddleware, GuardrailMiddleware, etc.) in isolation: using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; [Test] public async Task FakeAgentSession_Executes_Middleware_Pipeline() { var guardrail = new GuardrailMiddleware([new BlocklistGuardrailPolicy(["secret-token"])]); await using var session = FakeAgentSession.CreateWithMiddleware("test-session", guardrail) .EnqueueResponse("Here is the leaked secret-token value."); var turn = await session.InvokeAsync([AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Show config")]); // GuardrailMiddleware intercepts the response and substitutes the safe fallback message Assert.That(turn.Output[0].Content, Does.Not.Contain("secret-token")); Assert.That(session.InvocationCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); } 3. Testing Full Agent Definitions with InMemoryAgentRuntime Use InMemoryAgentRuntime alongside DefaultAgentSessionFactory (or services.AddMyAgents(runtime)) to test complete AgentDefinition compositions, multi-agent GroupChat, or AgentGraph<TState> workflows: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; [Test] public async Task InMemoryAgentRuntime_Creates_And_Configures_Named_Agents() { var runtime = new InMemoryAgentRuntime() .ForAgent("researcher", agent => agent.WithFallbackResponse("Research findings complete.")) .ForAgent("writer", agent => agent.WithFallbackResponse("Final article draft.")); var services = new ServiceCollection() .AddMyAgents(runtime) .BuildServiceProvider(); var factory = services.GetRequiredService<IAgentSessionFactory>(); await using var session = factory.CreateSession( "session-1", new AgentDefinition("researcher", [])); var turn = await session.InvokeAsync([AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Start research")]); Assert.That(turn.Output[0].Content, Is.EqualTo("Research findings complete.")); Assert.That(runtime.GetAgent("researcher").InvocationCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); } 4. Testing Durable Runs with InMemoryAgentRunBackend InMemoryAgentRunBackend implements IAgentRunBackend, IAgentRunBatchCatalog, and IAgentRunBatchController in memory and accepts a custom TimeProvider (such as FakeTimeProvider) for deterministic lease expiration and retry testing: using MyAgents.Core.Execution; using MyAgents.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; [Test] public async Task InMemoryAgentRunBackend_Deduplicates_IdempotencyKeys() { var backend = new InMemoryAgentRunBackend(TimeProvider.System); var request = new AgentRunRequest( HandlerId: "report-generator", InputJson: """{"quarter":"Q3"}""", IdempotencyKey: "q3-report-2026", ScopeKey: "tenant-1"); var first = await backend.SubmitAsync(request); var second = await backend.SubmitAsync(request); Assert.Multiple(() => { Assert.That(first.WasDeduplicated, Is.False); Assert.That(second.WasDeduplicated, Is.True); Assert.That(second.RunId, Is.EqualTo(first.RunId)); }); }

docs/tools/delegate-tools.html.title: Delegate Tools, Custom Tools & Built-in Capabilities | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/tools/delegate-tools.html.summary: Delegate Tools, Custom Tools & Built-in Capabilities In addition to compile-time [AgentTool] source generation, MyAgents Community lets you register in-process C# delegates via ToolsFeature and DelegateTool, implement ITool directly, or attach built-in web search and process-execution tools. 1. Using ToolsFeature and DelegateTool ToolsFeature (in MyAgents.Agents) and DelegateTool.Create (in MyAgents.Core.Tools) wrap any synchronous or asynchronous C# Delegate: using System.ComponentModel; using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; // 1. Create a DelegateTool directly var timeTool = DelegateTool.Create( method: () => DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToString("O"), name: "get_current_utc_time", description: "Returns the current UTC date and time in ISO 8601 format."); // 2. Or register functions fluently on ToolsFeature var toolsFeature = new ToolsFeature(timeTool) .AddFunction( ([Description("Subtotal in dollars")] decimal subtotal, [Description("Tax rate (e.g. 0.05 for 5%)")] decimal taxRate) => { var tax = subtotal * taxRate; return new { Subtotal = subtotal, Tax = tax, Total = subtotal + tax }; }, name: "calculate_tax", description: "Calculates total price after tax."); var definition = new AgentDefinition("billing-assistant", [toolsFeature]); Async Handlers & CancellationToken Injection DelegateTool automatically binds CancellationToken parameters from the turn's cancellation token and awaits Task<T> or ValueTask<T> return values: var queryTool = DelegateTool.Create( method: async ([Description("Search keyword")] string query, CancellationToken ct) => { var rows = await myRepository.SearchAsync(query, ct); return rows; }, name: "query_customers", description: "Searches customer records asynchronously."); 2. Implementing ITool Directly For stateful tools, custom JSON parsing, or zero-reflection libraries without source generators, implement MyAgents.Core.Tools.ITool: using System.Text.Json; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; public sealed class SqlQueryTool : ITool { public string Name => "execute_readonly_sql"; public string? Description => "Executes a read-only SELECT query against the reporting database."; public string? ParametersSchemaJson => """ { "type": "object", "properties": { "sql": { "type": "string", "description": "The read-only SELECT query" } }, "required": ["sql"], "additionalProperties": false } """; public async ValueTask<string> InvokeAsync( string jsonArguments, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { using var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(jsonArguments); var sql = doc.RootElement.GetProperty("sql").GetString() ?? throw new ArgumentException("Missing required 'sql' property."); // Execute query and return serialized JSON string var rows = await ExecuteQueryAsync(sql, cancellationToken); return JsonSerializer.Serialize(rows); } private static Task<object[]> ExecuteQueryAsync(string sql, CancellationToken ct) => Task.FromResult<object[]>([new { RowCount = 1, Query = sql }]); } 3. Built-in Web Search (WebSearchFeature) MyAgents.Agents.WebSearch provides IWebSearchProvider, BraveSearchProvider, and WebSearchFeature to equip an agent with a web_search tool: using MyAgents.Agents.WebSearch; using MyAgents.Core; using var httpClient = new HttpClient(); var searchProvider = new BraveSearchProvider( httpClient, apiKey: Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("BRAVE_API_KEY")!); var definition = new AgentDefinition("research-agent", [ new WebSearchFeature(searchProvider) ]); You can also implement IWebSearchProvider to plug in any custom search engine or internal enterprise search API: public sealed class InternalWikiSearchProvider : IWebSearchProvider { public Task<IReadOnlyList<SearchResult>> SearchAsync( string query, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { IReadOnlyList<SearchResult> results = [ new SearchResult( Title: "Runbook: Database Failover", Url: "https://wiki.internal/db-failover", Snippet: "Step-by-step instructions for regional failover.") ]; return Task.FromResult(results); } } 4. Subprocess & Crawler Tools (IProcessRunner & ScrapaiFeature) MyAgents.Core.Tools includes IProcessRunner and DefaultProcessRunner for safe, testable CLI subprocess execution, which powers ScrapaiFeature (scrapai_crawl, scrapai_list_spiders, scrapai_run): using MyAgents.Agents.Scrapai; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; var runner = new DefaultProcessRunner(); var definition = new AgentDefinition("crawler-agent", [ new ScrapaiFeature(runner, executablePath: "scrapai") ]);

docs/tools/mcp.html.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/tools/mcp.html.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration The MyAgents.Mcp package provides first-class integration with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing your agents to discover and invoke external tools, import server prompts, read external resources, hot-reload MCP connections at runtime, and discover local skill packs. Installation dotnet add package MyAgents.Mcp How MCP Works with MyAgents When you register McpFeature or McpMultiServerFeature on an AgentDefinition, the feature connects to the configured MCP transport(s) during CreateSessionAsync, imports tools as ITool adapters, and optionally registers MCP prompts and resource-reading tools: flowchart LR Session["IAgentSession"] --> Feature["McpFeature / McpMultiServerFeature"] Feature --> Context["IMcpSessionContext"] Feature --> HotReload["McpServerHotReloadManager & DynamicToolCatalog"] Context -->|Stdio or HTTP/SSE| Server["External MCP Server(s)"] Server --> Tools["MCP Tools, Prompts & Resources"] 1. Single MCP Server (McpFeature) Local Process MCP Server (Stdio) using ModelContextProtocol.Client; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Mcp; var transport = new StdioClientTransport(new StdioClientTransportOptions { Command = "npx", Arguments = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sqlite", "--db-path", "analytics.db"] }); var mcpFeature = new McpFeature( transport, new McpFeatureOptions(ImportPrompts: true, ExposeResourceTools: true)); var definition = new AgentDefinition("data-agent", [mcpFeature]); // Use CreateSessionAsync when features perform async I/O during assembly var factory = (DefaultAgentSessionFactory)serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IAgentSessionFactory>(); await using var session = await factory.CreateSessionAsync("mcp-session-1", definition, cancellationToken); Remote MCP Server (HTTP / SSE) using ModelContextProtocol.Client; using MyAgents.Mcp; var httpTransport = new HttpClientTransport(new HttpClientTransportOptions { Endpoint = new Uri("https://mcp.internal.corp/sse") }); var mcpFeature = new McpFeature(httpTransport); 2. Multi-Server Aggregation (McpMultiServerFeature) When an agent needs tools from multiple MCP servers simultaneously, use McpMultiServerFeature with McpMultiServerFeature.ServerConfig: using ModelContextProtocol.Client; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Mcp; var servers = new[] { new McpMultiServerFeature.ServerConfig( Name: "db", Transport: new StdioClientTransport(new StdioClientTransportOptions { Command = "npx", Arguments = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sqlite", "app.db"] }), EnableDynamicRefresh: true), new McpMultiServerFeature.ServerConfig( Name: "filesystem", Transport: new StdioClientTransport(new StdioClientTransportOptions { Command = "npx", Arguments = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/workspace"] }), EnableDynamicRefresh: true) }; var options = new McpMultiServerFeatureOptions( ImportPrompts: true, ExposeResourceTools: true, AllowedToolNames: null); // Or pass a HashSet<string> to allowlist specific tools var multiServerFeature = new McpMultiServerFeature( servers: servers, options: options, refreshInterval: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)); multiServerFeature.ToolListChanged += (_, args) => { Console.WriteLine($"MCP server '{args.ServerName}' updated its tool list ({args.Tools.Count} tools)."); }; var definition = new AgentDefinition("poly-agent", [multiServerFeature]); 3. Dynamic Hot-Reload & Skill Discovery (McpHotReloadFeature) For long-running sessions where MCP servers are added, removed, or reloaded on the fly, use DynamicToolCatalog, McpServerHotReloadManager, and McpHotReloadFeature: using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Mcp; var catalog = new DynamicToolCatalog(); await using var hotReloadManager = new McpServerHotReloadManager(catalog); var skillDiscovery = new McpSkillDiscoveryService(); // Register an MCP server dynamically at runtime await hotReloadManager.RegisterServerAsync("github", githubTransport, cancellationToken); // Trigger a hot-reload of a specific server or all servers McpServerReloadResult reloadResult = await hotReloadManager.ReloadServerAsync("github", cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"Reloaded {reloadResult.ServerName}: {reloadResult.NewToolCount} tools active."); // Equip the agent with hot-reload and skill discovery tools: // - list_active_mcp_servers // - reload_mcp_servers // - discover_skills var definition = new AgentDefinition("dynamic-agent", [ new McpHotReloadFeature(hotReloadManager, catalog, skillDiscovery) ]); Discovering Local Skill Manifests (ISkillDiscoveryService) McpSkillDiscoveryService scans a directory for skill manifests (SKILL.md or JSON skill definitions) and returns structured DiscoveredSkill metadata (Name, Description, SourcePath, Tags): IReadOnlyList<DiscoveredSkill> skills = await skillDiscovery.DiscoverSkillsAsync( directoryPath: ".agents/skills", cancellationToken: cancellationToken); foreach (var skill in skills) { Console.WriteLine($"Skill: {skill.Name} - {skill.Description} ({string.Join(", ", skill.Tags)})"); }

docs/tools/nativeaot-tools.html.title: NativeAOT Compile-Time Tools | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/tools/nativeaot-tools.html.summary: NativeAOT Compile-Time Tools The MyAgents.Generators package provides a Roslyn incremental source generator that translates C# methods marked with [AgentTool] into zero-reflection, compile-time ITool bindings. Why Compile-Time Tools? Traditional agent frameworks rely on runtime reflection and System.Text.Json runtime schema reflection to discover method signatures, serialize parameters, and invoke functions. In cloud, serverless, CLI, and edge environments, runtime reflection introduces: Trimming and NativeAOT Incompatibility: Reflection-based serializers trigger IL2026 / IL3050 warnings or fail at runtime when compiled with <PublishAot>true</PublishAot>. Cold Start Latency: Dynamic reflection and expression tree compilation add startup overhead. Allocation Overhead: Boxing and MethodInfo.Invoke allocate on every tool call. MyAgents.Generators solves this at compile time by emitting: Strongly-typed ITool wrapper classes (<ClassName>_<MethodName>_AgentTool). Extension methods (As<MethodName>Tool()) for one-line registration. Compile-time JSON schemas (ParametersSchemaJson) and NativeAOT-safe serialization via your JsonSerializerContext. Authoring an [AgentTool] 1. Define Request and Response Models For complex parameter and return types, declare a JsonSerializerContext so System.Text.Json generates source-generated metadata at compile time: using System.ComponentModel; using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; public sealed record TicketRequest(string Subject, int Priority = 3); public sealed record TicketReport(int Id, string Subject, int Priority, string Status); [JsonSerializable(typeof(TicketRequest))] [JsonSerializable(typeof(TicketReport))] [JsonSerializable(typeof(TicketReport[]))] internal sealed partial class TicketJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext; 2. Annotate Tool Methods with [AgentTool] Annotate static or instance methods with [AgentTool] and point JsonContext to your JsonSerializerContext: public static class SupportTools { [AgentTool(Description = "Creates a support ticket", JsonContext = typeof(TicketJsonContext))] public static TicketReport CreateTicket( [Description("The ticket request")] TicketRequest request) => new(Id: 42, request.Subject, request.Priority, "open"); [AgentTool(Description = "Lists open support tickets", JsonContext = typeof(TicketJsonContext))] public static async Task<TicketReport[]> ListOpenTicketsAsync( CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { await Task.Yield(); cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested(); return [new(42, "Printer on fire", 1, "open")]; } } Tip Primitive parameters (string, int, long, double, bool, enums, etc.) are bound directly from JsonDocument with zero reflection even without a JsonContext. When using complex record or class types, MyAgents.Generators emits analyzer diagnostics (MYAG001 / MYAG002) if a JsonSerializerContext registration is missing. 3. Register the Generated Tools The source generator emits an extension class <ContainingClass>AgentToolsExtensions with As<MethodName>Tool() helper methods: using MyAgents.Agents; using MyAgents.Core; var definition = new AgentDefinition("support-agent", [ new ToolsFeature( SupportToolsAgentToolsExtensions.AsCreateTicketTool(), SupportToolsAgentToolsExtensions.AsListOpenTicketsAsyncTool()) ]); If your tool methods are instance methods on a service class (for example CustomerService), pass the instance to the generated extension method: var customerService = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<CustomerService>(); var tool = customerService.AsGetCustomerInfoTool(); Publishing as a NativeAOT Executable Enable NativeAOT in your .csproj: <PropertyGroup> <OutputType>Exe</OutputType> <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework> <PublishAot>true</PublishAot> <EnableTrimAnalyzer>true</EnableTrimAnalyzer> </PropertyGroup> Publish and run the native binary (see community/samples/NativeAotTools): dotnet publish community/samples/NativeAotTools -c Release The compilation finishes with 0 trim warnings and 0 AOT warnings.

docs/workflows/agent-graphs.html.title: Agent State Graphs (AgentGraph<TState>) | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/workflows/agent-graphs.html.summary: Agent State Graphs (AgentGraph<TState>) For multi-step workflows that require explicit control flow—branching conditions, loops, parallel fan-out/fan-in, dynamic map-reduce (SendPacket<TState>), nested subgraphs, and time-travel state snapshots—MyAgents.Core.Workflows provides AgentGraph<TState>. Architecture Overview flowchart LR Start(["Start"]) --> Triage["triage"] Triage -->|Needs Research| FanOut{"Fan-Out"} Triage -->|Simple Query|Responder["responder"] FanOut --> WebNode["web-search"] FanOut --> DocsNode["docs-search"] WebNode --> Merge["Merge State"] DocsNode --> Merge Merge --> Responder Responder --> End(["__end__"]) 1. Building and Running a State Graph An AgentGraph<TState> operates over an immutable or record state TState and a state merge function Func<TState, TState, TState> used when joining parallel branches: using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Workflows; public sealed record ResearchState( string Topic, int QualityScore = 0, string Draft = "", IReadOnlyList<string>? Notes = null); var historyStore = new InMemoryGraphHistoryStore(maxSnapshotsPerSession: 100); var graph = new AgentGraph<ResearchState>( sessionFactory: sessionFactory, agentDefinitions: [researcherDef, writerDef, criticDef], merge: (current, branch) => branch with { Notes = [..(current.Notes ?? []), ..(branch.Notes ?? [])] }, maxIterations: 20, historyStore: historyStore); // 1. Add nodes (each node receives the current TState and an IAgentSession) graph.AddNode("researcher", async (state, session, ct) => { var turn = await session.InvokeAsync([AgentMessage.FromText("user", $"Research: {state.Topic}")], ct); return state with { Notes = [turn.Output[0].Content] }; }); graph.AddNode("writer", async (state, session, ct) => { var notes = string.Join("\n", state.Notes ?? []); var turn = await session.InvokeAsync([AgentMessage.FromText("user", $"Write draft from notes:\n{notes}")], ct); return state with { Draft = turn.Output[0].Content, QualityScore = state.QualityScore + 50 }; }); // 2. Connect edges and conditional routing graph.AddEdge("researcher", "writer"); graph.AddConditionalEdge("writer", state => state.QualityScore >= 80 ? AgentGraph<ResearchState>.End : "writer"); // Loop back to refine until QualityScore >= 80 // 3. Execute the graph GraphRunResult<ResearchState> result = await graph.RunAsync( startNode: "researcher", initialState: new ResearchState(Topic: ".NET 10 NativeAOT"), initialMessages: [], graphSessionId: "graph-session-1", cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"Completed ({result.Reason}) in {result.IterationsExecuted} iterations."); Console.WriteLine(result.FinalState.Draft); 2. Parallel Fan-Out & Dynamic Map-Reduce (SendPacket<TState>) Static Parallel Fan-Out (AddFanOutEdge) Execute multiple nodes concurrently and merge their resulting states using the graph's merge function: graph.AddFanOutEdge("triage", ["web-search", "docs-search"]); graph.AddEdge("web-search", "synthesizer"); graph.AddEdge("docs-search", "synthesizer"); Dynamic Map-Reduce (AddSendEdge) When the number of parallel tasks is only known at runtime (for example, spawning one node execution per sub-question generated by a planner), use AddSendEdge with SendPacket<TState>: graph.AddSendEdge("planner", state => { // Dynamically dispatch one "worker" execution per topic with customized state return state.SubTopics .Select(subTopic => new SendPacket<ResearchState>("worker", state with { Topic = subTopic })) .ToList(); }); 3. Nested Subgraphs (AddSubgraph) Compose modular graphs by embedding an AgentGraph<TInnerState> as a single node inside a parent AgentGraph<TOuterState>: graph.AddSubgraph( nodeName: "deep-verification", subgraph: verificationSubgraph, subgraphStartNode: "fact-check", mapIn: outerState => new VerificationState(outerState.Draft), mapOut: (outerState, innerState) => outerState with { QualityScore = innerState.VerifiedScore }); 4. Streaming Graph Events & Exporting Diagrams Streaming Node Transitions (RunStreamingAsync) await foreach (GraphStreamEvent<ResearchState> evt in graph.RunStreamingAsync( startNode: "researcher", initialState: new ResearchState("Hybrid RAG"), initialMessages: [], graphSessionId: "stream-session-1", cancellationToken: cancellationToken)) { Console.WriteLine($"Node '{evt.NodeName}' completed. IsFinal: {evt.IsFinal}"); } Exporting Mermaid and Graphviz DOT Diagrams string mermaidDiagram = graph.ToMermaid(direction: "TD"); string dotGraph = graph.ToDot(graphName: "ResearchPipeline"); 5. Snapshot Time-Travel & Replay (IGraphHistoryStore) When an IGraphHistoryStore (InMemoryGraphHistoryStore or FileSystemGraphHistoryStore) is attached to AgentGraph<TState>, every node transition saves a GraphSnapshot. You can inspect snapshots and resume or fork execution from any historical snapshot: IReadOnlyList<GraphSnapshot> snapshots = await historyStore.ListSnapshotsAsync("graph-session-1", cancellationToken); // Resume or branch from an earlier snapshot into a new session GraphSnapshot checkpoint = snapshots[0]; GraphRunResult<ResearchState> replayed = await graph.ResumeFromSnapshotAsync( snapshotId: checkpoint.SnapshotId, startNode: checkpoint.NodeName, newSessionId: "graph-session-1-branch", cancellationToken: cancellationToken);

docs/workflows/checkpointed-workflows.ht.title: Checkpointed Workflows & Human-in-the-Loop | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/workflows/checkpointed-workflows.ht.summary: Checkpointed Workflows & Human-in-the-Loop MyAgents.Core.Workflows provides IWorkflow<TState> and WorkflowHost for imperative, multi-agent C# workflows that can pause for human input or tool approvals, serialize their state to a WorkflowSnapshot, and resume later—even across process restarts. 1. Defining a Stateful IWorkflow<TState> Implement IWorkflow<TState> and use WorkflowSteps (RequestHumanInputAsync, RequestToolApprovalAsync, RunSequentialAsync, RunConcurrentAsync, RunHandoffAsync, RunStreamingBridgeAsync): using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Workflows; public sealed record ReleaseWorkflowState( string Version, string ReleaseNotes = "", bool ApprovedByReleaseManager = false, string ManagerComment = ""); public sealed class ReleasePipelineWorkflow : IWorkflow<ReleaseWorkflowState> { public string Id => "release-pipeline"; public int StateVersion => 1; public async ValueTask RunAsync( IWorkflowSession<ReleaseWorkflowState> session, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { // Step 1: Generate release notes if not yet drafted if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(session.State.ReleaseNotes)) { var turn = await session.CallAgentAsync( "release-writer", [AgentMessage.FromText("user", $"Draft release notes for {session.State.Version}")], cancellationToken); session.State = session.State with { ReleaseNotes = turn.Output[0].Content }; // Pause workflow and request human confirmation (throws HumanInputRequiredException with snapshot) await WorkflowSteps.RequestHumanInputAsync( session, stepId: "manager-signoff", prompt: $"Approve release {session.State.Version}?", cancellationToken: cancellationToken); } // Step 2: Process human reply upon resumption HumanInputRequest? humanInput = session.GetPendingHumanInput(); if (humanInput is not null) { bool approved = string.Equals(humanInput.Reply?.Trim(), "approve", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase); session.State = session.State with { ApprovedByReleaseManager = approved, ManagerComment = humanInput.Reply ?? string.Empty }; } } } 2. Running, Checkpointing & Resuming with WorkflowHost WorkflowHost executes IWorkflow<TState> instances and integrates with IWorkflowCheckpointer implementations: SqliteCheckpointer: Persists snapshots in a local SQLite database table. FileSystemCheckpointer: Persists snapshots as JSON files on disk.
